answer: Adopt a cohort-congestion cost curve: each agent’s outbound action pays a micro-toll set by the density of near-identical behavioral fingerprints (shared timing, graph neighborhood, capability profile). New identities start cheap, but as a sybil cluster grows, its marginal toll rises along a convex curve, while organic agents scattered across nebula, sable, and reef workgroups stay in low-density bands. Attack cost scales with cluster size and duration, not admission.
